overview.en: Jane Jacobs was an American-Canadian journalist, author, and activist who influenced urban planning with her critique of modernist city design.

early_life.en: Jacobs was born in Scranton, Pennsylvania. She worked as a journalist in New York and became an influential voice in urban studies without formal academic training.

impact.en: Jacobs's The Death and Life of Great American Cities challenged prevailing urban planning orthodoxy and championed the vitality of diverse, walkable neighborhoods.

event.en: Published The Death and Life of Great American Cities
Moved to Toronto to avoid Vietnam draft for her sons
Published Cities and the Wealth of Nations

title.en: The Death and Life of Great American Cities

description.en: Revolutionary critique of modern urban planning

text.en: Cities have the capability of providing something for everybody, only because, and only when, they are created by everybody.

quotes.source: The Death and Life of Great American Cities
